item.title: Musical chairs: The Tipline for 4 February 2026
item.description: Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson is taking on a second job. CBS reported on Wednesday that President Trump will establish a new anti-fraud task force led by Vice President JD Vance, with Ferguson serving as vice chair while remaining head of the FTC. item.title: It’s go time: The Briefing for 5 February 2026
item.description: India’s Competition Commission appears to dislike flight cancellations as much as the consumers it serves. Yesterday, the agency revealed it is investigating IndiGo based on concerns that the country’s leading airline unlawfully pulled thousands of flights from departure boards to create artificial scarcity in the market. Also in The Briefing, Google’s AI Overviews are accused of breaching new mea...

item.title: Two years on – how amended regulations have impacted strategic investments in Chinese companies
item.description: Revisions to measures on strategic investments in China have established a relaxed qualification threshold, expanded the definition of a ‘foreign investor’ and made changes in investment methods. The amended measures are designed to expand the market, lower barriers for foreign investors and encourage foreign investments in Chinese companies.

item.title: EU official bats back calls to launch FSR probe into US airline subsidies
item.description: Complaints that historic multi-billion-dollar government support packages to US airlines potentially fall afoul of the EU’s Foreign Subsidies Regulation are likely time-barred, a senior European Commission official has said.

item.title: Boies Schiller Flexner lands first EU-based antitrust partner
item.description: Boies Schiller Flexner has launched an EU-based competition practice, bolstering its partnership with a lateral hire from Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton in Italy.

item.title: German enforcer issues first-ever disgorgement order to Amazon
item.description: Amazon has vowed to appeal against a newly-announced German infringement decision ordering the company to repay €59 million in economic benefits earned as a result of an abuse of dominance breach.

item.title: Cardell: Cloud services up for consideration in soon-to-be-proposed SMS probe
item.description: The cloud services sector is one of several options under consideration as the UK’s Competition and Markets Authority prepares for a potential fourth strategic market status investigation, according to its chief executive.

item.title: Google seeks to quash €76 million Belgian penalty
item.description: Google has urged a Belgian appellate court to ignore competition law arguments from an advertising start-up, as the technology company seeks to quash a €76 million penalty for failing to restore access to its ad exchange for over three days.

item.title: Arm and a leg: The Tipline for 5 February 2026
item.description: Medtronic is on the hook for $382 million for illegally monopolising certain blood vessel instruments through bundling and exclusive dealing. The 10-day trial concluded on Friday, with the California federal jury accepting the damages estimate of Applied Materials’ hired expert, Econic Partners founder Jon Orszag. item.title: Whistleblower bar expecting wave of antitrust work after first award
item.description: The rapid rollout and promotion of the Department of Justice’s new antitrust informant regime has whistleblower specialists anticipating an influx of work.
